title: When the Harvest Breaks
premise: Isandro Blackwood takes a teaching post in the dying farm town of Hollow Creek, where a class of students vanished in 1974 and no one will say how. When mirrors begin lagging reality by one second, Isandro realizes the town's prosperity was bought with those children — fed, year after year, to something living under the fields. With three students who can still remember fragments of the missing class, Isandro descends beneath the harvest to return what was taken. The ending costs them: they free the children's souls but must surrender their own memories of everyone they've come to love, waking as a stranger among people who grieve them without knowing why.
about_author: J. M. Underhill is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent nine years in farming communities that never quite explained their empty desks. They write horror about institutions, inheritance, and the quiet violence of small towns keeping their ledgers balanced.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Arriving in Hollow Creek, Isandro inherits a classroom with nineteen desks and twenty-three names on the 1974 memorial plaque outside. The principal warns them not to ask about 'the gap year.' Emotional beat: uneasy curiosity; documentation as armor against a town that prefers forgetting.

chapters.title: The Second Behind
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. A student, Marisol, mentions her bathroom mirror 'waits for her.' That night Isandro's own reflection lags — a blink arriving late, a smile held too long. They begin a log. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into obsession; the comfort of record-keeping curdling into compulsion.

chapters.title: Nineteen Desks
chapters.summary: POV alternating Isandro and Marisol. In the school basement archive, Isandro finds 1974 attendance records with pages razored out, and a teacher's journal describing 'the tithe.' Marisol admits she dreams in a child's handwriting she's never learned. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery shadowed by grief that isn't theirs.

chapters.title: What the Fields Eat
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The harvest is impossibly abundant while neighboring farms fail. An old farmer, drunk, tells Isandro the town 'pays in kind' and that his brother was 'the first payment.' That night every mirror in Isandro's rented house shows the room one full second behind. Emotional beat: isolation deepening; the house itself becomes hostile witness.

chapters.title: Found Family
chapters.summary: POV Marisol. Marisol, Dev, and quiet Theo — the only students who remember fragments — bond with Isandro over stolen archives and burnt dinners. Theo draws the missing class from memory, faces accurate down to freckles. Emotional beat: warmth blooming against horror; found family forming precisely because the town has abandoned its dead.

chapters.title: The Tithe Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The journal reveals the arrangement: since 1974, four children per generation, given below the fields at first frost, in exchange for harvests and the town's survival. The next payment is due in eleven days — and the ledger lists four names, all current students. Emotional beat: cold clarity; documentation finally becomes indictment.

chapters.title: Below the Stubble
chapters.summary: POV alternating Isandro and Dev. Following Theo's drawings to a collapsed root cellar, the group finds the threshold: soil that breathes, and voices reciting attendance like a prayer. The thing below speaks in the missing teacher's voice, offering Isandro a place in the ledger instead of the children. Emotional beat: terror laced with temptation — survival offered at someone else's price.

chapters.title: First Frost
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The town, complicit and desperate, moves to collect the payment early; parents who once befriended Isandro bar their doors. Marisol is taken during the harvest festival. Isandro chooses descent over safety, carrying the ledger and the returned names. Emotional beat: betrayal and resolve; the price of survival made literal and personal.

chapters.title: Return What Was Taken
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Beneath the fields, time pools like water — 1974 never ended there. Isandro reads the names aloud, refusing the bargain of replacement, offering instead their own memories as payment: every recollection of Hollow Creek, of Marisol, Dev, and Theo. The children's souls pass through the breaking mirrors toward morning. Emotional beat: sacrificial climax; love expressed as willing erasure.

chapters.title: The Stranger Who Stayed
chapters.summary: POV Marisol. Spring comes. Four long-dead names are added to the memorial as 'found,' and Marisol, Dev, and Theo wake whole but hollowed by a grief they can't source. A new teacher named Blackwood arrives with no memory of them, only an inexplicable habit of documenting everything — and a logbook whose last entry reads: worth it. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; memory lost, family somehow still felt.
